name: Argemone

project_scope.local_taxonomic_note: Argemone albiflora is the parent species concept. The Central Texas learner represents the local field target as Argemone albiflora subsp. texana; do not create a duplicate parent-species card. A. polyanthemos and A. sanguinea are learner-approved represented comparison taxa even while their target-zone native-range labels remain unresolved.

genus_diagnostics.habit: Spiny annual or biennial herbs with glaucous foliage.
genus_diagnostics.leaves: Alternate, deeply lobed, with sharp marginal teeth/spines and often prickles on veins.
genus_diagnostics.sap: Colored latex is useful but not sufficient across all four represented taxa: A. aurantiaca is orange to reddish-orange, while the other represented taxa have yellow/pale-yellow latex.
genus_diagnostics.flower: Large showy flowers with numerous stamens. Petal color is only a first-pass cue: A. albiflora subsp. texana, A. aurantiaca, and A. polyanthemos are normally white; A. sanguinea can be white or lavender.
genus_diagnostics.sepals: Three caducous sepals forming a prickly bud, each with a horn-like tip.
genus_diagnostics.fruit: Prickly capsule; prickle length, branching, and density are diagnostic.

quick_key.if: Fresh latex is orange to reddish-orange; sepal horns 8–12 mm and prickly; capsule prickles very unequal, often branched, longest about 15–35 mm
Latex yellow/pale-yellow; upper leaf surface unarmed; sepal horns 6–10(–15) mm and usually unarmed; capsule surface plainly visible between widely spaced prickles, longest 4–10(–12) mm
Latex yellow; petals white or lavender; proximal leaves lobed to about 4/5 toward midrib; sepal horns 5–10 mm and slightly prickly basally; capsule prickles unequal, longest 5–7(–10) mm
Fresh latex pale/light yellow; sepal horns about 4–6(–10) mm and usually unarmed; capsule prickles mostly simple and shorter, longest about 6–10(–12) mm

study_warning: Do not identify these four from petal color alone. A. sanguinea may be white or lavender, and the other three are commonly white. Start with fresh latex, then upper leaf-surface armature, bud/sepal horns, and mature capsule prickles.

priority: mature capsule prickle length and branching
b073_study_strategy.warning: Do not separate the two local core species by petal color: both are white-flowered. Use fresh latex plus mature capsule and bud characters.

quick_split: A. albiflora subsp. texana — white petals; fresh latex pale/light yellow; sepal horns usually 4–6(-10) mm and mostly unarmed; mature capsule prickles mostly simple and much shorter, with the longest about 6–10(-12) mm.
A. aurantiaca — white petals; fresh latex orange to reddish-orange; sepal horns 8–12 mm and prickly; mature capsule prickles very unequal, often branched, with the longest about 15–35 mm.
A. polyanthemos — white- to pale-lavender-flowered plains/west-central look-alike; HOLD for target-zone range and use mature fruit/bud characters.
A. sanguinea — rose/red/lavender-flowered South Texas look-alike; HOLD pending exact target-zone county evidence.

local_field_key.aurantiaca: very unequal, often branched; longest about 15–35 mm

shared_traits: alternate sessile leaves with spine-tipped teeth
large flowers with caducous horned sepals
study_strategy.warning: Petal color, overall plant height, and generic 'spikiness' overlap. A. sanguinea can flower white, and A. polyanthemos overlaps A. albiflora subsp. texana strongly in white petals, yellow latex, and short capsule prickles.

visual_comparison.title: Prickly poppy: look at the weapons, not the petals
visual_comparison.subtitle: These two Central Texas plants both flower white. The capsule and sap are far more useful.
visual_comparison.memory_rule: Yellow sap = albiflora. Orange sap = aurantiaca.

visual_comparison.overlay_note: Arrows and labels are learner-generated overlays; they are not part of the original photographs.

look_here_first: 1. Nick fresh tissue only when appropriate and note latex color.
2. Inspect the upper leaf blade itself, not just margins/veins: A. polyanthemos is characteristically unarmed adaxially.
3. Photograph an unopened bud side-on and measure the sepal horn; note whether the horn itself is prickly.
4. Use a mature capsule side view to compare prickle spacing, equality, branching, and maximum length.

species_differences.argemone-albiflora-subsp-texana: Pale/light-yellow latex; sepal horns about 4–6(–10) mm, usually unarmed; mature capsule prickles mostly simple, longest about 6–10(–12) mm.
species_differences.argemone-aurantiaca: Orange to reddish-orange latex; prickly 8–12 mm sepal horns; mature capsule prickles very unequal, often branched, longest about 15–35 mm.
species_differences.argemone-polyanthemos: Upper leaf surface unarmed; buds 15–22 × 10–15 mm; terete sepal horns 6–10(–15) mm, usually unarmed; capsules 35–50 × 10–17 mm with widely spaced prickles, longest 4–10(–12) mm.
species_differences.argemone-sanguinea: Upper leaf surface unarmed to sparingly prickly on main veins; buds 12–20 × 10–15 mm; sepal horns 5–10 mm, slightly prickly basally; petals white or lavender; capsules 25–40(–50) × 8–15(–18) mm with unequal prickles, longest 5–7(–10) mm.
